importantNotes: Genesis means 'beginning' or 'origin' — it is the book of beginnings.
Contains the first messianic prophecy (Genesis 3:15) — the 'proto-evangelium'.
The Abrahamic Covenant (Gen 12, 15, 17) is foundational to the entire Bible.
Joseph's story foreshadows Christ: rejected by his brothers, exalted to save many.
Genesis covers more time than all other books of the Bible combined.

chapters.1: God creates the heavens, the earth, light, sky, seas, vegetation, stars, animals, and humanity in six days.
chapters.2: God forms Adam from dust and Eve from Adam's rib; He places them in the Garden of Eden.
chapters.3: The serpent tempts Eve; Adam and Eve eat the forbidden fruit and are expelled from Eden.
chapters.4: Cain murders his brother Abel out of jealousy; God marks Cain and sends him away.
chapters.5: The genealogy from Adam to Noah, recording the long lifespans of the early patriarchs.
chapters.6: Humanity's wickedness grows; God instructs Noah to build an ark to survive the coming flood.
chapters.7: Noah, his family, and the animals enter the ark; the great flood covers the earth.
chapters.8: The floodwaters recede; Noah sends out a dove; they leave the ark and Noah builds an altar.
chapters.9: God makes a covenant with Noah, symbolized by the rainbow; the curse of Canaan.
chapters.10: The Table of Nations — the descendants of Noah's sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
chapters.11: The Tower of Babel — God confuses languages; genealogy from Shem to Abram.
chapters.12: God calls Abram to leave his homeland; the Abrahamic Covenant is initiated.
chapters.13: Abram and Lot separate; Lot chooses the fertile plain near Sodom.
chapters.14: Abram rescues Lot from captivity; Melchizedek blesses Abram.
chapters.15: God makes a formal covenant with Abram, promising countless descendants.
chapters.16: Sarai gives Hagar to Abram; Ishmael is born.
chapters.17: God renames Abram to Abraham and Sarai to Sarah; circumcision is instituted.
chapters.18: Three visitors promise Abraham a son; Abraham intercedes for Sodom.
chapters.19: God destroys Sodom and Gomorrah; Lot's wife becomes a pillar of salt.
chapters.20: Abraham deceives Abimelech about Sarah being his sister.
chapters.21: Isaac is born to Abraham and Sarah; Hagar and Ishmael are sent away.
chapters.22: God tests Abraham by asking him to sacrifice Isaac; God provides a ram instead.
chapters.23: Sarah dies; Abraham purchases the cave of Machpelah for her burial.
chapters.24: Abraham's servant finds Rebekah as a wife for Isaac.
chapters.25: Abraham dies; Esau sells his birthright to Jacob for a bowl of stew.
chapters.26: Isaac prospers in Gerar; God reaffirms the covenant with Isaac.
chapters.27: Jacob deceives Isaac and steals Esau's blessing with Rebekah's help.
chapters.28: Jacob's dream of a ladder reaching heaven at Bethel; God confirms the covenant.
chapters.29: Jacob works for Laban; he marries Leah and then Rachel.
chapters.30: Jacob's children are born; he prospers and plans to return home.
chapters.31: Jacob flees from Laban; they make a covenant at Mizpah.
chapters.32: Jacob wrestles with God at Peniel and is renamed Israel.
chapters.34: Dinah is violated; Simeon and Levi take violent revenge on Shechem.
chapters.35: God reaffirms Jacob's new name Israel; Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin.
chapters.36: The genealogy of Esau and the Edomites.
chapters.37: Joseph's dreams anger his brothers; they sell him into slavery in Egypt.
chapters.38: Judah and Tamar — the story of Judah's daughter-in-law.
chapters.39: Joseph serves in Potiphar's house; he is falsely accused and imprisoned.
chapters.40: Joseph interprets the dreams of Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker in prison.
chapters.41: Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dreams of famine; he is made ruler over Egypt.
chapters.42: Joseph's brothers come to Egypt to buy grain; Joseph recognizes them.
chapters.43: The brothers return to Egypt with Benjamin; Joseph hosts a feast.
chapters.44: Joseph tests his brothers by hiding a silver cup in Benjamin's sack.
chapters.45: Joseph reveals his identity to his brothers and forgives them.
chapters.46: Jacob and his family move to Egypt; God reassures Jacob in a vision.
chapters.47: Jacob's family settles in Goshen; Joseph manages the famine in Egypt.
chapters.48: Jacob blesses Joseph's sons Ephraim and Manasseh.
chapters.49: Jacob gives prophetic blessings to each of his twelve sons.
chapters.50: Jacob dies and is buried in Canaan; Joseph forgives his brothers and dies in Egypt.
